speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a longstanding pruritic rash with numbness and tingling on your palms; to begin our evaluation, have you noticed if this rash appears symmetrically on both hands, and does it have a specific color or texture?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of an itchy rash on his upper body and face. Additionally, he has been experiencing a numbness and tingling sensation on both palms. He has been working on his family's rice farm, also caring for livestock.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient describes a year-long itchy rash on the upper body and face, along with numbness and tingling in both palms while working on a rice farm with livestock. To differentiate between occupational dermatoses like pompholyx or scabies and other conditions, can you tell me if the rash involves the web spaces between your fingers or the sides of your nails, and do you have a similar rash on your feet or wrists?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_Hands

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC). The combination of pruritus, palm paresthesia (likely due to carpal tunnel syndrome from the rash), and a history of occupational exposure to wood dust or solvents strongly suggests this autoimmune liver disease. I am requesting antimitochondrial antibody (AMA) testing to confirm.
